creature: Observed male Joppa farmers and convert; shared race fitting

resident.description:
He is a wind-carved man with the posture of a vinereaper; his spine is bent to point the bright turquoise of his eyes at the tilling angle, his hips are pushed odd-forward with the slumping ease of a stance much more relaxed than his. If it weren't for the salt on his brow and the scarred knuckles, he would seem a marble Saad perched under a crumbling tomb.
{{C|-----}}
Loved by {{C|the villagers of Joppa}}.

Disliked by {{C|the Seekers of the Sightless Way}} for leading a raiding party on one of their camps.

Disliked by {{C|mysterious strangers}} for torching one of their villages.

The tatters of a sweat-stained kufiya thrash in the wind from where they hang about the farmer's neck. Clasped in his gnarled, brown hand is a curved vinereaper of iron with which he culls moisture-swollen wafers from the viridian plant called watervine.

source_resolution: Runtime and installed description agree on wrought-iron crescent for watervine. Actual head/shaft form follows glyph; shaft material not explicitly stated, so no wood grain or bindings are invented.

donor_reference.role: Actual current Hatchet texture, identified by VWE_MeleeWeapon_Axe definition and LoadFolders1.6/1.7. Flat single-handed head/shaft scale and outline reference, not Qud shape replacement. Prior female construction used installed legacy Axe.png, which is not the current def texPath.

rejected_reference.role: Inspected flint sickle; composite chipped teeth and bent wooden handle conflict with wrought-iron crescent. Not selected.

design: Forged crescent head with open inner curve and simple straight shaft; same tool in every facing. Head mounted at shaft end; restrained edge shading. No teeth, wraps, wood grain, gems or invented farmer costume.
authored_scale: Approximately380 source pixels /36 pixels in48x96 preview. Authored readable scale, not dimension inferred from weight.

frame.camera: Strict SEN body; stationary upright/diagonal authoring display, not ready/drafted pose. Back mirrors unmarked blade surface to show opposite side. West mirrors profile.

palette.detail_assignment: Original differentiates head and shaft masks but maps both to native y. Preserve separate material regions without inventing a new color.
